chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in a man enjoying (temporary marriage) with a Jewish woman and a Christian woman, while he has a free (non-slave) woman."

key_terms.حُرَّةٌ: a free woman (as opposed to a slave or concubine)
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعَ: to enjoy (specifically referring to temporary marriage or mut'ah in this context)

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim man practice temporary marriage with Jewish or Christian women while married to a free Muslim or non-Muslim woman?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the permissibility of temporary marriage (mut'ah) with women of the Book is not restricted by the man's existing marital status with a free woman, distinguishing it from permanent marriage rules. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the conditions for mut'ah are distinct, allowing a man to maintain a permanent free wife while simultaneously contracting mut'ah with a Jewish or Christian woman. This highlights the flexibility of mut'ah as a separate legal category within Shia fiqh, independent of the exclusivity often associated with permanent nissah.
